title: Sourdough Loaf
subtitle: a slow-fermented loaf with a crisp crust and open crumb
excerpt: Real sourdough takes two days and an active starter. The reward is a loaf with a crackling crust, chewy crumb, and a depth of flavour that commercial bread cannot match. This recipe assumes you already have a starter that has been fed and is actively bubbling.
sourceNotes: Based on traditional European naturally leavened bread techniques.

recipe.freezeNotes: Slice and freeze. Reheat slices in a toaster or warm oven.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cold-prove overnight in the fridge for up to 16 hours. Bake straight from cold.
recipe.temperatureNote: Conventional oven, very hot. Use a heavy lidded pot such as a cast iron casserole.

content.text: This recipe requires an active sourdough starter -- feed it 8 to 12 hours before baking so it is at peak activity. You will know it is ready when it is doubled in size and full of bubbles. The long cold prove develops flavour and makes the loaf easier to score.

items.prepNote: use 300ml warm water -- plus 50ml extra if dough feels stiff

content.text: In a large bowl combine 100g of your active starter with 300ml warm water. Stir to dissolve. Add the flour and mix until no dry flour remains. Cover and leave for 30 minutes (autolyse).
Sprinkle over the salt. Squeeze it through the dough with wet hands until fully incorporated. Perform 4 sets of stretch and folds over the next 2 hours, spaced 30 minutes apart.
Leave the dough to bulk ferment at room temperature for 4 to 6 more hours until it has grown by 50 to 75 percent and feels airy.
Turn out, pre-shape into a round, rest 20 minutes, then do a final shape. Place seam-side up in a floured proving basket (banneton) or a bowl lined with a floured cloth.
Cover and refrigerate overnight or for up to 16 hours. Heat the oven to 240C with a heavy lidded pot inside.

Turn the cold dough onto baking paper. Score the top with a sharp blade. Lower into the hot pot, put the lid on, and bake for 20 minutes. Remove the lid and bake for a further 25 minutes until deep brown. Cool fully before cutting.

items.cause: Starter was not active enough, or the dough over-fermented.
items.fix: Your starter should pass the float test -- drop a small spoonful into water; if it floats, it is ready. If it sinks, feed it and wait longer.

items.cause: Oven or pot was not hot enough, or the lid was removed too early.
items.fix: Preheat the pot for at least 45 minutes. Keep the lid on for the full first 20 minutes of baking.

content.text: Sourdough is older than commercial yeast by thousands of years. Every culture with a grain tradition has some version of it. The modern British sourdough revival drew on San Francisco baking culture, French pain de campagne, and German sauerteig. The result is a loaf that has become a weekend ritual for home bakers across the country.
